note: Real public-web research on the category and audience. The business itself is fictional.

findings.text: Pew (2015): 54% of parents of kids ages 6-17 said their children took music, dance or art lessons in the past 12 months; about one in three parents of children 5 or younger said the same. Rates were higher in families earning $75k+ (62%) than under $30k (41%).
findings.source_title: Parental attitudes on children’s extracurricular activities

findings.text: Ages 5-11 are the main window: in a Gallup survey for NAMM, 64% of respondents began musical training between ages 5 and 11, and 18% between 12 and 14.
findings.source_title: Gallup Organization Reveals Findings of "American Attitudes Toward Making Music" Survey

findings.text: Parents support starting early: in a 2015 NAMM Foundation survey of 800 parents and 1,000 teachers, 81% of parents said children should have a chance to learn a musical instrument as early as elementary school.
findings.source_title: Striking A Chord: The Public's Hopes and Beliefs for K-12 Education in the United States: 2015

findings.text: Word of mouth carries weight: Nielsen's 2015 Global Trust in Advertising survey found 83% of respondents completely or somewhat trust recommendations from friends and family, the most trusted form of advertising.

Free trial lessons are a common offer in the category. NAMM recommends lesson programs consider them; a typical trial combines the lesson, a facility tour, and time to answer parents' questions, with sign-up at the end.
findings.source_title: The Benefits of Offering Trial Lessons

findings.text: Recitals double as retention and marketing: music retailers running lesson programs told a NAMM session that recitals are a proven way to keep good students, and that student performance nights are among their busiest nights.
findings.source_title: Music Lessons: Your Big Questions Answered

findings.text: Instagram says Reels are built for discovery: most of what people see in Reels comes from accounts they don't follow. Its top ranking signals are how likely a viewer is to reshare, watch to the end, like, or open the audio page.
